Ben — good questions, thank you. Short answers up front, followed by artifacts and pointers.

1) NAT/egress behavior: The terraform module provides two supported modes (controlled-egress and proxy-egress).
   - controlled-egress: egress allowed only via explicit IP ranges (NAT gateways with SGs) — this is the default for priv deployments.
   - proxy-egress: egress routed to an outbound proxy cluster (sidecar or dedicated proxy pool). If the proxy fails, the fail-closed option blocks egress; fail-open is explicitly opt-in.
   We recommend controlled-egress + explicit proxy for SaaS integrations that require outbound connectivity. See module README in the zip (modules/network/egress.md).

2) Flow logs: VPC flow logs are shipped to a customer-managed S3 bucket (or object store) and optionally forwarded to your SIEM. Default retention is 180 days; retention policy is configurable via variables.tf (module variable: flow_log_retention_days). We include a lifecycle rule in the terraform module.

3) GitLab CI enforcement: We enforce merge-blocking via protected branch settings + pipeline-level status checks. Key pipeline jobs: infra-validate, policy-scan (OPA), secret-scan (trufflehog), and manifest-sign. The pipeline is configured to require all jobs to pass for the protected branch. You can see the job names and sample pipeline at: https://gitlab.redwood.com/redwood/priv-deploy/-/pipelines/4123 (link shared above).

4) Key rotation: The playbook uses our KM integration layer which supports cloud KMS or HSM connectors. Rotation is orchestrated by ansible-runner with a default 90-day window; a canary rotation is performed on non-prod before production rollover. Integration notes are in ansible-playbooks/README.md in the zip.

Artifacts provided in this email: short extracts from the Terraform module README and the GitLab job list.

Sanjay (ACME FYI): we also included the helm-values override that pins egress policies in the service mesh — please review.

If Thu 3/4 10:00 PT works, we'll send a calendar invite and a short runbook for the dry run.

—Soojin

Ben / team — adding a couple of implementation notes from module ownership perspective: 

- Module owners: modules/network (Soojin), modules/egress (me), modules/kms (Irene). I'll own the `egress` module's gating behavior changes (fail-closed default).
- CI hooks: infra-validate runs `terraform validate` + plan-diff against a golden state; policy-scan runs OPA against plan output. We also have a manifest-sign step which produces a signed artifact stored in the pipeline artifact store for reproducible deploys.
- Rollforward: if a policy-scan fails unexpectedly during a rollout, pipelines are configured to auto-abort and open a backfill ticket to HBSP-4982.

I reviewed the ansible playbook — two small asks: add an idempotence check at the end of the run (ansible --check) and include a sentinel file write on successful rotation so auditors can query rotation history without parsing logs. I'll push a branch with these two minimal changes by EOD.

Karthik
